title: RS_LazyTile
description: Splits a raster into unpadded tiles, preserving OutDb bands as lazy source windows.
kernels:
  - returns: list
    args:
    - raster
    - name: width
      type: integer
    - name: height
      type: integer
  - returns: list
    args:
    - raster
    - name: band_indices
      type: array
    - name: width
      type: integer
    - name: height
      type: integer
---

::: callout-warning
**Experimental.** This function is experimental; its behavior may change without notice.
:::

## Description

`RS_LazyTile(raster, [band_indices,] width, height)` returns a list of
`{x, y, tile}` structs in row-major order. Grid positions are zero-based;
band indices are one-based and preserve the requested order. Width and height
must be positive. Edge tiles are smaller when the dimensions do not divide
evenly. Padding and nodata fill options are not supported; use
[RS_Tile](rs_tile.qmd) when padding is required.

OutDb bands retain their source URI and a composed view without reading pixels.
Retiling a tile composes its window with the existing view. InDb bands copy
their tile pixels. Tile geotransforms shift to each tile's origin.

A single `UNNEST(RS_LazyTile(...))` can use `RasterTileExec` to emit bounded
batches, limited by execution batch size and estimated tile pixel bytes
(`sedona.raster.max_batch_bytes`). An oversized tile is emitted alone.
Scalar list consumers and multiple zipped unnests build the full list, but
OutDb tiles remain lazy.

Metadata filters can discard tiles before downstream pixel-consuming functions
load their windows. `RS_EnsureLoaded(tile)` requests loading explicitly.
Source pushdown is not yet implemented.
